modules.module_title: Sweep and Clean Parking Area, Escalator Area and Club House

pcs.pc_description: sweep the parking area to remove dirt, leaves, and other debris that accumulate on the surface.
Pick up litter and trash scattered throughout the parking area to maintain cleanliness and prevent potential hazards.
Clean any stains, oil spills, or other substances that may have leaked or accumulated on the ground.
Carry out periodic power washing of the parking area to remove stubborn stains and dirt, improving the overall appearance.
Empty and sanitize trash bins placed in the parking area to prevent overflowing and maintain hygiene.
Sweep sidewalks and curbs adjacent to the parking area to ensure a neat and tidy appearance.
Remove weeds and maintain the landscaping in the parking area to prevent overgrowth and enhance the overall aesthetic.
Ensure that lighting fixtures in the parking area are clean and functional, providing adequate visibility and safety for users.
wipe down handrails and balustrades to remove dirt, grease, and germs of the escalator area
Clean the escalator steps by vacuuming or sweeping to remove dirt, dust, and debris.
Clean and wipe down the skirting and comb plates at the top and bottom of the escalator.
Clean the glass panels around the escalator to maintain transparency and appearance.
Polish metallic parts of the escalator to keep them looking clean and well-maintained.
inspect the escalator for any damages or malfunctioning parts and reporting them for timely repair.
Check that safety signs and instructions are visible and in good condition.
Apply non-slip coatings to the escalator steps to enhance safety.
Ensure the escalator pit is free from debris and clutter for safe and efficient operation.
Empty the water tanks before cleaning to ensure safe access for cleaning personnel.
Carry manual removal of sediment, sludge, leaves, and debris that may have accumulated at the bottom of the tank.
carry physical scrubbing of the inner surfaces of the tank using appropriate brushes or scrubbers to remove algae, biofilm, and other contaminants.
Use high-pressure water jets to clean the tank walls and corners effectively.
Apply a suitable disinfectant to eliminate any remaining bacteria, viruses, or harmful microorganisms.
rinse the tank with clean water to remove any residual cleaning agents and disinfectants.
Inspect the tank for any cracks, leaks, or structural damage that may require repair.
Fill the tank with clean and potable water once cleaning and inspection are completed.
Conduct water quality tests to ensure the water meets safety standards before reintroducing it into the building's water supply system.
Evaluate the condition of the facade to identify areas with heavy soiling, mold, algae, or stains.
Cover surrounding areas, windows, and entrances to protect them from cleaning agents and debris.
Remove loose dirt, dust, and debris from the facade's surface using brushes, brooms, or compressed air.
Use appropriate cleaning solutions and detergents, or pressure washing, to clean the facade's surfaces thoroughly.
Apply specific treatments or solvents to remove stubborn stains, graffiti, or other blemishes.
Treat areas affected by algae, mold, or mildew with appropriate cleaning agents to prevent their regrowth.
Rinse the facade with clean water to remove cleaning agents and residues.
Apply protective coatings or sealants to enhance the facade's resistance to dirt, moisture, and UV rays.
